problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation  ${f}^{′}(x)=\frac{3}{x-1}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution of a Differential Equation Using Integration
examples.problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $f'(x) - 3\sin(2x) = 0.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation to give

$$
f'(x) = 3\sin{2x}.
$$

Then, we integrate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int 3\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\ f(x) & =3\int \operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
